newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: UN body urges push to target big drug dealers.
newsitem.headline: UN body urges push to target big drug dealers.

text.p: Criminal justice systems around the world should direct their energies and resources into targeting big-time drug dealers instead of users and pushers, the United Nation's drugs agency said on Tuesday.

The Vienna-based International Narcotics Control Board (INCB) said in its annual report that "the immense economic power" of transnational crime syndicates posed a major threat to police, judiciary and politicians and should be tackled at an international level.

"The Board suggests that countries set a higher priority on apprehending and punishing high-level criminals. For persons convicted of possessing small amounts of illicit drugs, alternatives to prison sentences should be considered."
Drug production, trafficking and abuse had spread to previously unaffected areas, aided by the opening up of global borders, the report noted.
The board voiced concern over a rising world trend in the abuse of synthetic drugs such as Ecstasy and weight-reducing pills.
"Among the problems highlighted are emerging illicit markets for anorectic stimulants...and a rapid spreading of abuse of amphetamines, mainly of Ecstasy," the INCB said.

Widespread abuse of appetite suppressants, often believed to offer a quick fix for obesity and other psychological disorders, had been reported from a number of countries, but in particular from Argentina, Brazil, Chile and the U.S.
"The Board received reports citing health clubs, fashion shops and beauty farms as places where such drugs can be illicitly obtained," it noted.
The INCB warned the adverse reactions to such pills ranged from heightened blood pressure to violent behaviour and paranoia.

It noted that there was a "clear upward trend" in the abuse of synthetic drugs manufactured in clandestine laboratories in Europe, which were supplying amphetamines and "Ecstasy" pills to illegal drug markets in Europe and outside of the continent.
The agency added that large amounts of heroin and cocaine continued to be smuggled into western Europe, but that the abuse of such substances in the region had declined.
